findings.evidence: evaluate_with sets self.disabled for every non-cancel provider error, including ExprErrorCode::Budget. With one shared Fuel in PropertyStore, a property can exhaust the allowance and leave a later property with Budget. That later property's expression then stays disabled (sticky) on all later ticks, even though the cause was transient and came from another property. The spec basis for disabling on a resource budget, as opposed to a script error, was not verified.
findings.remediation: Treat Budget as a per-evaluation fallback (no sticky disable) or cite the MOT rule that requires disable

findings.evidence: The deadline is enforced only inside HostBridge::checkpoint/charge/read. MotionJsProvider::evaluate never compares clock.now_ns() against deadline_ns after engine.run returns. An adapter that runs past the deadline without calling checkpoint still has its value accepted. Fuel has the same cooperative shape, so the adapter's guarantee is only as strong as each engine's checkpoint discipline.
findings.remediation: Add a post-run now_ns()>deadline_ns check mapping to Budget(Deadline); document engine checkpoint obligation

findings.evidence: The production public API exports ScriptedEngine, a command-word test double and not JavaScript. The lane honestly declares JS engine evaluation NOT_PROVEN. Every quota, fuel, recursion and memory behaviour is proven only against this double, and the double enforces recursion and memory itself. The adapter does not prove those two.
findings.remediation: Gate ScriptedEngine behind a test-support feature; keep NOT_PROVEN until a real engine adapter passes the same suite

Accord already owns Ticks::checked_sub/checked_add/Ord since b1fe6e8, an ancestor of 87c1cd9. The lane's accord_requests note is stale. Later commit 28d8ed4 (not in the reviewed commit) drops them.

findings.evidence: `delivered = deliver_end - start` underflows when the request starts past the truncation point (start > available_samples, want_end <= declared). Debug builds panic; release returns Truncated{delivered: ~2^64}. Probe: 1000 declared frames, file cut at 300, request 320..330. Re-verified by the round lead.
findings.remediation: Return Truncated{delivered:0} or OutOfRange when start >= available; use checked_sub; add probe test

findings.evidence: `token.split_at(1)` on validated UTF-8 header tokens panics when the first char is multi-byte. Example: header token 'é' is reachable via Registry::detect->probe. A crafted file crashes the caller instead of returning typed Corrupt. Re-verified by the round lead.
findings.remediation: Take tag via token.as_bytes()[0] / split_at_checked; non-ASCII tag -> Corrupt

findings.evidence: In the moov branch, `pos + size > file_len` is an unchecked add on a 64-bit largesize. It panics in debug; in release it wraps and misreports. The sibling branch uses checked_add. Re-verified by the round lead.
findings.remediation: Use pos.checked_add(size).filter(|e| *e <= file_len) else Corrupt{moov-exceeds-file}

findings.evidence: build_presentation starts each edit at the first sample with pts >= media_time. The sample whose interval contains media_time is dropped. Example: AAC elst media_time 2112 over 1024-sample frames skips frame 2048, so presentation runs 960 samples late and seek(0) is OutOfRange. Tests only use aligned media_time.
findings.remediation: Start at last sample with pts <= media_time, clamp its presented pts; add unaligned-edit test

findings.evidence: Index expands each track to one SampleEntry per sample, with one shared max_samples budget (4M). A QuickTime PCM track (one sample per PCM frame) at 48 kHz longer than ~83 s makes the whole MOV fail LimitExceeded, so video seek fails too. Out of scope: later commit 3bfc100 claims a compact PCM index.
findings.remediation: Compact run-length index for constant-size/duration tracks or per-track budget

findings.evidence: Reel reimplements these pulse-owned conversions: media_to_ticks with NearestHalfUp and exact flag (pulse ticks_from_rational_seconds), the Y4M F-tag fps->FrameRate (pulse frame_rate_from_fps), fps_fraction, and ticks-per-sample. The allow-list forbids reel->pulse, so the shared owner belongs in accord.
findings.remediation: Hoist timescale->tick rounding and fps<->FrameRate helpers into accord; pulse and reel consume them

findings.evidence: The module doc claims QuickTime sound v2 is typed Unsupported. In the code, parse_stsd parses only version <= 1 and sets audio=None for v2 with no error, so the track indexes silently.
findings.remediation: Return Unsupported{quicktime-sound-v2} for v2 sample entries or correct the doc

findings.evidence: Y4M decode never checks start against complete_frames. A request past the end of a complete file returns Truncated{0} (Loss), while WAV returns OutOfRange in the same case.
findings.remediation: Return OutOfRange when the file is record-aligned and want_end > complete_frames

findings.evidence: proxy_usable probes the original before its grant is verified. decode_packets accepts a prebuilt MediaIndex with no content_id/revision/len binding, so an index can be replayed against a different same-length file.
findings.remediation: Verify grant before probe; bind content_id+revision+len into MediaIndex and check in decode_packets

findings.evidence: Weak oracles: colr is tested only with (1,1,1,false) and pasp only with (1,1), so swapped fields would pass. ctts v1, negative offsets, elst v1 and largesize are never exercised. pub mod fixtures ships test byte builders in the public API.
findings.remediation: Use asymmetric colr/pasp values, add ctts-v1/elst-v1/largesize cases, gate fixtures behind a feature

findings.evidence: RampedGain::process polls cancel before `self.before = self.current`, and Chain::reset (chain.rs:182-184) resets every stage, including stages that never ran. Sequence: block A ramps 0->1 and publishes, then block B is canceled in stage 0 (current reverts to 0), then block C re-ramps 0->1 where flat 1.0 was expected. That is a 0.75 step, which breaks 'a changed volume never steps'. Re-verified by the round lead.
findings.remediation: Record before/committed value prior to any early return; add chain cancel-then-continue ramp test

findings.evidence: The output count comes from rubato 5.0.1 process_all_into_buffer, which uses ceil(f64 ratio*len). For 44100->48000 with 44100 frames, 1.0884353741496597*44100 = 48000.00000000001, so 48001 frames are published while the exact u128 request is 48000. end_sample then overlaps the next clip by one sample. Re-verified by the round lead (python + rubato lib.rs:330).
findings.remediation: Publish exactly the u128 requested count (trim and report tail) or refuse; test 44.1k->48k @44100 frames

findings.evidence: InputBlock::validate rejects only rate 0 or > 768000. A rate that does not divide TICKS_PER_SECOND (e.g. 47999) is processed and published, and only receipt start_ticks()/end_ticks() fail afterwards.
findings.remediation: Call ticks_per_sample(rate) and end-tick conversion during admission, before any write

findings.evidence: On discard, HardLimiter and Equalizer reset to their initial state, not the last-published state. The resubmitted block therefore starts with a 341-sample delay-line gap and zeroed EQ history, which can click.
findings.remediation: Snapshot state at publish into preallocated buffers and restore on discard, or document dropout

findings.evidence: Gain::new and mix send levels are only finite-checked. Large values (f32::MAX gain) publish +inf samples and an inf peak, and nothing checks the output is finite.
findings.remediation: Bound gain/send to the authored range or refuse non-finite output before publish
